## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 4 (*Jatumaṭṭhaka*, "Using a dildo") is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a Buddhist nun who uses a dildo (*jatumaṭṭhaka*) commits a confession-entailing infraction [SuttaCentral; Hirakawa 1982]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Comparative Vinaya studies connect this rule with parallel legislation across other early Buddhist schools. SuttaCentral identifies direct parallels in the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pc 4) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pc 4), the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya (Chinese Bi Vb Pc 73 and Bi Pm Pc 73), the Mahīśāsaka Vinaya (Chinese Bi Vb Pc 72 and Bi Pm Pc 72), the Sarvāstivāda Vinaya (Chinese Bi Vb Pc 85 and Bi Pm Pc 85), and the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya in both Chinese and Tibetan versions (Bi Vb Pc 94 and Bi Pm Pc 94) [SuttaCentral]. Akira Hirakawa additionally notes the rule's correspondence to the Mahāsāṃghika Bhikṣuṇī Vinaya's regulation against making and using dildos [Hirakawa 1982].

Within the Pali canon, the DharmaNexus database detects 147 internal text-reuse passages shared across 57 texts, driven predominantly by standardized procedural and legal formulas shared with other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga chapters [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial formulaic overlaps occur with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 3 (over 1,700 shared characters, prominently at §1.13–1.20) and several other Pācittiya rules, including Pc 2, Pc 6, Pc 55, and Pc 89 [DharmaNexus].
